A TV with sound but no picture (or completely black screen) can be frustrating, but it’s often caused by simple settings or connection issues rather than a major hardware failure. Here is a step-by-step troubleshooting guide to help you diagnose and fix the problem:

### 1. Check the Basics
• Is the backlight working? Turn off the lights in the room and shine a flashlight closely at the screen. If you can faintly see images or menus, your backlight has failed. This usually requires professional repair.
• Volume/Sound: Do you still have sound? If yes, the TV is on but not displaying video. If no, the TV may be in standby mode or completely dead.
• Input Source: Press the "Input," "Source," or "TV/Video" button on your remote. Make sure it’s set to the correct port (e.g., HDMI 1, HDMI 2) where your device is connected.

### 2. Check Cables and Connections
• HDMI/Component Cables: Unplug and firmly reconnect all video cables at both the TV and the external device (cable box, gaming console, streaming stick). Try a different HDMI cable if possible.
• Power Cycle Everything: Turn off the TV and all connected devices. Unplug them from power for 60 seconds. Plug them back in and turn them on. This resets the handshake between devices.

### 3. Test with Different Sources
• If you’re using a cable box, game console, or streaming device: Try connecting a different device (like another HDMI source) to see if the picture appears.
• If the TV has built-in apps (Netflix, YouTube, etc.): Open one of these directly on the TV. If you get an image from the built-in apps but not from external devices, the issue is with your external device or cable, not the TV screen.

### 4. Check for Physical Damage
• Look closely at the screen for cracks, lines, or discoloration. If you see vertical/horizontal lines or a shattered screen, the LCD/OLED panel is damaged and will need replacement.

### 5. Perform a Factory Reset (If Possible)
• If you can access the TV’s menu (even if the picture is dim), try performing a Factory Reset. This clears out any software glitches causing display issues.
• Note: If the screen is completely black, you may need to use your physical buttons on the TV (not the remote) to navigate or reset it.

### 6. Consider Hardware Failure
If none of the above works:
• Backlight Inverter/LED Strips: Common in older LCD TVs. The screen looks black but has sound. Fixable by a technician.
• Main Board or T-Con Board: These control image processing. If faulty, they may need replacement.
• Power Supply Unit: May not be sending enough power to the display panel.

### When to Call for Help:
• The TV is under warranty → Contact the manufacturer.
• You’re uncomfortable opening the TV → Hire a professional repair service.
• The cost of repair exceeds 50% of a new TV’s price → Consider replacing the TV.

Let me know what brand/model your TV is and whether you have sound, and I can give more specific advice!
Samsung, sound works fine. Torch shows menu faintly.

This confirms that your backlight has failed. The LCD panel and mainboard are working correctly (since you have sound and can see the menu with a flashlight), but the LEDs or CCFL tubes behind the screen are no longer illuminating it.

Here’s what to do next:

### 1. Quick Diagnostic Test
• Press Menu on your remote. If you can faintly see the menu overlay when shining a light, this is 95% likely a backlight issue.
• Listen for any clicking or buzzing sounds from the TV—this can indicate a failing inverter board (on older CCFL models) or driver circuitry.

### 2. Warranty Check
• If your Samsung TV is under warranty (usually 1–3 years depending on region), contact Samsung Support immediately. Do not attempt repairs yourself, as this will void the warranty.
• If you purchased an extended warranty, check its terms for backlight coverage.

### 3. Repair Options (If Out of Warranty)
Backlight repair is common and often cost-effective compared to replacing the entire TV. You have two main options:

#### Option A: Professional Repair
• Contact a local TV repair shop or Samsung Authorized Service Center.
• Cost Estimate: Typically $150–$400, depending on screen size and model.
• Ask if they can replace just the backlight strips/LEDs rather than the entire panel (which is more expensive).

#### Option B: DIY Repair (For Technically Inclined Users)
• Risk: High. Requires disassembling the TV, which involves handling fragile glass panels and electrical components. Incorrect reassembly can damage the screen permanently.
• Steps:
  1. Find your exact Samsung model number (on a sticker on the back of the TV).
  2. Search YouTube for “[Your Model Number] backlight replacement” to see if it’s feasible.
  3. Order replacement LED strips or CCFL tubes from sites like PartsExpert, RepairClinic, or eBay.
  4. Follow a detailed guide carefully.

### 4. When to Consider Replacement
• If the TV is older than 5–7 years, repair costs may approach the price of a new budget model.
• If the screen itself is cracked or has dead pixels beyond the backlight issue, replacement is usually more economical.

### Summary
Your TV’s core electronics are fine—only the lighting system failed. This is a very common and fixable issue. If under warranty, contact Samsung. If not, get a quote for professional backlight repair before deciding to replace the TV.
